questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah, one of the many leaders of 1857, moved from village to village preaching against the British with a drum. He was popularly known as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Danka Shah
Why: He was known as Danka Shah, the maulvi with the drum (danka).
Why not the others: (A) Shah Mal led at Barout. (B) Gonoo led at Singhbhum. (C) Nana Sahib led at Kanpur.
Key point: Religious leaders and prophets helped spread the message of revolt.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, the Congress held about ____ of the seats.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 82%
Why: The Congress held about 82% of the seats in the Assembly.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are the wrong share.
Key point: The Congress itself included members with very different views, so debates were vigorous.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: To make the Congress a mass organisation in the 1920s, Gandhi encouraged it to set up committees based on:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Linguistic regions
Why: New branches were set up on the basis of linguistic regions, so that the Congress could work in people's own languages.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) would have divided people. (D) The princely states had their own Praja Mandals.
Key point: Gandhi also encouraged leaders to speak to people in their mother tongue.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Site)
(A) Sanchi
(B) Ajanta
(C) Ellora
(D) Barabar

List-II (Monument)
(I) The Kailashnatha temple, carved out of a single rock
(II) Caves cut for the Ajivikas
(III) A stupa with carved gateways
(IV) Cave paintings of Jataka stories
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Sanchi has a stupa with carved gateways (III). Ajanta has paintings of Jataka stories (IV). Ellora has the monolithic Kailashnatha temple (I), and Barabar the caves cut for the Ajivikas (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Sanchi and Ajanta. (C) swaps Ajanta and Ellora. (D) swaps Ellora and Barabar.
Key point: Together these sites show the range of early religious architecture.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Records from western India show that women sometimes petitioned the village panchayat. Their petitions often:
options: A) Asked for land revenue to be raised
B) Demanded posts as revenue officials
C) Sought to replace the muqaddam
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Complained of husbands' neglect
Why: Women petitioned the panchayat seeking justice, often complaining of husbands' infidelity or neglect of wife and children.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not what the records describe.
Key point: Such records show women using the institutions of the village to seek redress.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Hymns of the Rigveda praise many deities. Among the most important were:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Agni, Indra and Soma
Why: The Rigveda praises Agni (fire), Indra (a warrior god) and Soma (a plant from which a drink was made).
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are deities who became important in later Puranic traditions.
Key point: Vedic sacrifices were performed by heads of households and, later, by kings with elaborate rituals.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: In 1342, Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as his envoy to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) China
Why: Ibn Battuta was sent as the sultan's envoy to the Mongol ruler of China.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) were not his destination.
Key point: On the way, he travelled through Malabar, the Maldives and Sri Lanka.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: At Kalibangan, the ploughed field had two sets of furrows at right angles to each other. This suggests that:
options: A) The plough was pulled by horses
B) Two crops were grown together
C) The field was a temple ground
D) Canals were cut across the field
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Two crops were grown together
Why: Furrows at right angles suggest that two different crops were grown together in the field.
Why not the others: (A) There is no evidence of horse-drawn ploughs. (C) and (D) are not suggested by the furrows.
Key point: The field dates to the Early Harappan levels at Kalibangan.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Event)
(A) First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
(B) Objectives Resolution moved
(C) India becomes independent
(D) The Constitution comes into force

List-II (Date)
(I) 13 December 1946
(II) 15 August 1947
(III) 9 December 1946
(IV) 26 January 1950
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
Why: The Assembly first met on 9 December 1946 (III), and the Objectives Resolution was moved on 13 December 1946 (I). Independence came on 15 August 1947 (II), and the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 (IV).
Why not the others: (B) swaps the first meeting and the resolution. (C) swaps the resolution and independence. (D) swaps independence and the Constitution's date.
Key point: The Assembly worked for almost three years, across the transfer of power.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: How did members of the public take part in the work of the Constituent Assembly?
options: A) They voted on each article directly
B) They chose the Assembly's President
C) They sent suggestions that were debated
D) They elected the Drafting Committee
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) They sent suggestions that were debated
Why: The public sent suggestions and opinions, which the Assembly took into account in its debates.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not how the Assembly worked.
Key point: The debates were reported in newspapers, so arguments were also made in public.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.sub_topic: Symbol of the Paharias' way of life
questions.question: In contrast with the plough of the Santhals, the Paharias' way of life is often symbolised by the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hoe
Why: The Paharias used the hoe for shifting cultivation, while the Santhals used the plough.
Why not the others: (A) symbolises the Santhals. (C) and (D) are not the symbols used.
Key point: The two tools stand for two ways of life: shifting cultivation and settled agriculture.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Person)
(A) Lord Dalhousie
(B) Lord Canning
(C) Colin Campbell
(D) Lord Wellesley

List-II (Description)
(I) Devised the subsidiary alliance in 1798
(II) Commander whose forces relieved Lucknow
(III) Governor-General during the revolt, mocked for his leniency
(IV) Annexed Awadh in 1856
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Dalhousie annexed Awadh (IV). Canning was Governor-General in 1857 (III). Campbell commanded the relief of Lucknow (II), and Wellesley devised the subsidiary alliance (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Dalhousie and Canning. (B) swaps Canning and Campbell. (C) swaps Campbell and Wellesley.
Key point: British policies over half a century built up the grievances that burst out in 1857.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Abu'l Fazl, the author of the *Ain-i Akbari*, was a courtier and historian of the emperor:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Akbar
Why: Abu'l Fazl was Akbar's courtier and historian. The *Ain* forms part of his larger *Akbar Nama*.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were other Mughal emperors.
Key point: The *Ain* was meant to present a picture of Akbar's empire as well-ordered and prosperous.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Under the Permanent Settlement, the revenue demand on each zamindar was:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Fixed in perpetuity
Why: The revenue was fixed permanently, in perpetuity, so it would not rise in future.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) contradict the settlement. (B) Revenue was paid in cash.
Key point: The Company hoped a fixed demand would encourage zamindars to invest in the land.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The verses of the Chishti saint Shaikh Fariduddin Ganj-i Shakar (Baba Farid) were later included in the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) *Adi Granth*
Why: Baba Farid's verses were included in the *Adi Granth Sahib*.
Why not the others: (A) The *Bijak* has Kabir's verses. (B) The *Tevaram* has Nayanar hymns. (D) The *Kitab-ul-Hind* is al-Biruni's work.
Key point: The inclusion shows how devotional traditions shared ideas and audiences.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Jawaharlal Nehru
Why: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946.
Why not the others: (A) Prasad was President. (B) Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. (C) Patel worked mostly behind the scenes.
Key point: The resolution set out the defining ideals of the Constitution.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: The rumour about greased cartridges in 1857 concerned the cartridges of the new:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Enfield rifle
Why: The Enfield rifle's cartridges were rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were not the weapons in the rumour.
Key point: Sepoys had to bite the cartridges before loading, which made the rumour so alarming.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about zamindars in the Mughal period:
(A) Zamindars never supported revolts against the Mughal state.
(B) Zamindars could sell, bequeath or mortgage their milkiyat lands.
(C) Most zamindars had fortresses and armed contingents of cavalry, artillery and infantry.
(D) Zamindars helped colonise agricultural land and settle cultivators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (C) and (D) only
Why: (B), (C) and (D) follow NCERT. Zamindars controlled their lands, kept armed forces, and helped extend cultivation.
Why not the others: (A) is false. Zamindars often led or supported revolts, sometimes with peasant backing. Options (B), (C) and (D) include (A).
Key point: The zamindars' relationship with the state combined cooperation and conflict.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: In Sufi orders, the master who controlled a khanqah and guided disciples was known as a shaikh, a murshid or a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Pir
Why: The master was known as a shaikh, pir or murshid. He enrolled disciples (murids) and appointed a successor (khalifa).
Why not the others: (A) A murid was a disciple. (B) A qazi was a judge. (C) An alim was a scholar of Islamic studies.
Key point: The khanqah became a centre of social life for both the Sufis and their visitors.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.sub_topic: Terms for tribute, land and people
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Peshkash
(B) Jangli
(C) Milkiyat
(D) Miras or watan

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Tribute, which from forest chiefs often included elephants
(II) Zamindars' personal lands
(III) Artisans' hereditary land rights in Maharashtra
(IV) A term for people of the forest, who lived by gathering, hunting and shifting cultivation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: Peshkash was tribute (I), jangli the term for forest dwellers (IV), milkiyat zamindars' personal lands (II), and miras or watan artisans' hereditary rights (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps peshkash and jangli. (B) swaps jangli and milkiyat. (C) swaps milkiyat and miras.
Key point: These terms show how the state, landholders, artisans and forest people were linked.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Thinkers in the Upanishads tried to understand questions about life after death and rebirth, and ideas such as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Atman and Brahman
Why: The Upanishads explored atman, the individual self, and Brahman, the universal soul.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the subjects of the Upanishads.
Key point: The questions raised in the Upanishads were part of a wider debate that included the Buddha and Mahavira.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the problems al-Biruni saw in understanding India:
(A) Sanskrit was so different from Arabic and Persian that ideas could not easily be translated.
(B) Religious beliefs and practices differed from his own.
(C) He found the local population self-absorbed and insular.
(D) He found Sanskrit easy to learn and saw no barriers at all.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are the three barriers al-Biruni named: language, differences in religion, and the insularity of the local people.
Why not the others: (D) is false, because he found Sanskrit a major barrier. Option (A) leaves out the true statement (C), and options (B) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Al-Biruni overcame these barriers by relying heavily on Sanskrit texts.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's social programme:
(A) He worked to abolish untouchability.
(B) He believed that Hindu–Muslim unity was unimportant for swaraj.
(C) He promoted spinning and the wearing of khadi.
(D) He saw village self-reliance as central to his vision for India.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B) only
Why: Only (B) is false. Gandhi saw Hindu–Muslim unity as essential to swaraj and worked for it all his life.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: For Gandhi, swaraj meant social reform as well as political freedom.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: The confidential fortnightly reports on the political situation in the provinces were prepared by the British government's:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Home Department
Why: The Home Department prepared the fortnightly reports, based on information from the provinces.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) did not prepare these reports.
Key point: These reports show what officials saw and feared, and are read with that bias in mind.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Krishnadeva Raya wrote a work on statecraft in Telugu called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Amuktamalyada
Why: Krishnadeva Raya wrote the *Amuktamalyada* in Telugu.
Why not the others: (A) is a chronicle of Kashmir. (B) is Banabhatta's biography of Harsha. (D) is attributed to Kautilya.
Key point: In it, the king advises that ports should be improved and trade encouraged.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.sub_topic: Chronology of the Santhals in the Rajmahal hills
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) The Santhal Pargana is created
(B) Santhals begin coming into Bengal
(C) The number of Santhal villages reaches 1,473
(D) The Damin-i-Koh is marked out
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: The Santhals began coming into Bengal in the 1780s, and the Damin-i-Koh was marked out by 1832. Their villages numbered 1,473 by 1851, and the Santhal Pargana was created after the revolt of 1855–56.
Why not the others: (A) puts the Damin-i-Koh before their arrival. (C) puts the 1851 figure before 1832. (D) puts the Pargana before 1851.
Key point: The creation of the Santhal Pargana was meant to conciliate the Santhals after the revolt.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1869
Why: Gandhi was born in 1869.
Why not the others: (B) is the year of the revolt, (C) the year the Congress was founded, and (D) the year he went to South Africa.
Key point: Gandhi studied law in London before going to South Africa.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Harappan writing has been found on seals, copper tools, rims of jars, bone rods and even on:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) An ancient signboard
Why: NCERT notes that the script appears on many objects, including an ancient signboard.
Why not the others: (B) No Harappan temples have been identified. (C) Palm-leaf manuscripts belong to much later times. (D) The Harappans did not issue coins.
Key point: Most inscriptions are short, which is one reason the script has not been deciphered.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.sub_topic: From the Alvars' anthology to the Khalsa
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Shankaradeva preaches in Assam
(B) Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa
(C) Shaikh Ali bin Usman Hujwiri settles in Lahore
(D) The Alvars' compositions are compiled in the *Nalayira Divyaprabandham*
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (D), (C), (A), (B)
Why: The Alvars' compositions were compiled by the tenth century, and Hujwiri settled in Lahore in the eleventh century. Shankaradeva preached in the late fifteenth century, and the Khalsa was founded in 1699.
Why not the others: (B) puts Hujwiri before the compilation. (C) puts Shankaradeva before Hujwiri. (D) puts the Khalsa before Shankaradeva.
Key point: Hujwiri's tomb in Lahore, the Data Darbar, is still visited by pilgrims.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about jatis and guilds:
(A) Unlike the four varnas, the number of jatis was not fixed.
(B) An inscription from Mandasor records the history of a guild of silk weavers who moved there from Lata, in Gujarat.
(C) The Mandasor inscription says that the weavers built a temple to the sun god.
(D) Jatis were never organised into shrenis, or guilds.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. Groups that shared a craft were often organised into shrenis, as the Mandasor silk weavers were.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (C) and (D) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: The Mandasor inscription shows that guilds could migrate, prosper and act as patrons.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Ibn Battuta's book of travels, the *Rihla*, was written in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Arabic
Why: The *Rihla* was written in Arabic.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not its language.
Key point: The *Rihla* gives rich details of social and cultural life in the fourteenth century.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Bernier's works were published in France in ____, and within five years they were translated into English, Dutch, German and Italian.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1670–71
Why: Bernier's works were published in 1670–71 and soon translated into several European languages.
Why not the others: (B) is the time of Akbar's accession. (C) is the time of Plassey. (D) is the time of the Fifth Report.
Key point: Bernier's account was reprinted many times, and it shaped European ideas about India.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Saint)
(A) Basavanna
(B) Kabir
(C) Guru Nanak
(D) Mirabai

List-II (Teaching)
(I) Described the Ultimate Reality as one, using terms from many traditions
(II) Devotion to Krishna, defying the norms of her marital family
(III) Rejected sacrifices, ritual baths and image worship
(IV) Questioned caste and the idea of rebirth
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: Basavanna questioned caste and rebirth (IV). Kabir described one Ultimate Reality (I). Guru Nanak rejected sacrifices, ritual baths and image worship (III), and Mirabai was devoted to Krishna (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Basavanna and Kabir. (B) swaps Kabir and Guru Nanak. (D) swaps Guru Nanak and Mirabai.
Key point: These saints criticised ritual and stressed personal devotion.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Vijayanagara:
(A) The city had no walls and relied entirely on the river for defence.
(B) The fortifications enclosed agricultural land as well as the city.
(C) Domingo Paes described the city as being as large as Rome.
(D) Merchants called kudirai chettis took part in the horse trade.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false. Abdur Razzaq noted seven lines of fortification, and the walls were massive.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: Walls around fields meant the city could hold out during a long siege.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Field or method)
(A) Stratigraphy
(B) Palaeobotany
(C) Archaeozoology
(D) Archaeogenetics

List-II (What it studies)
(I) Ancient DNA
(II) The layers of a site
(III) Ancient plant remains
(IV) Animal remains
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: Stratigraphy studies the layers of a site (II), palaeobotany ancient plants (III), archaeozoology animal remains (IV), and archaeogenetics ancient DNA (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps stratigraphy and palaeobotany. (C) swaps palaeobotany and archaeozoology. (D) swaps archaeozoology and archaeogenetics.
Key point: Each method answers a different question about the Harappan past.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: At Vijayanagara, long streets lined with pillared verandahs ran from the temple gopurams. They are known as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Chariot streets
Why: These were chariot streets, along which temple chariots carried the deities in processions.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not the name used for them.
Key point: Merchants set up shops in the verandahs, so the streets were also centres of trade.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: The Kauravas, the hundred brothers led by Duryodhana, were the sons of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Dhritarashtra
Why: The Kauravas were the sons of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari.
Why not the others: (B) Pandu was the father of the Pandavas. (C) Drona was a teacher. (D) Shantanu belonged to an earlier generation.
Key point: Rival claims to the throne between the two sets of cousins led to the war.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: In April 1919, during the protests against the Rowlatt Act, troops opened fire on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Amritsar
Why: The firing took place at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are other cities.
Key point: The massacre deepened Indian anger against British rule.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.sub_topic: Chronology of the Buddha and his monuments
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Sanchi is rediscovered
(B) Images of the Buddha are made at Mathura
(C) The Buddha preaches his teachings
(D) A local raja stumbles upon the ruins at Amaravati
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: The Buddha preached in the sixth century BCE, and Buddha images were made at Mathura from about the first century CE. The Amaravati ruins were found in 1796, and Sanchi was rediscovered in 1818.
Why not the others: (A) puts the Mathura images before the Buddha. (B) puts Amaravati before the Mathura images. (C) puts Sanchi before Amaravati.
Key point: Amaravati was found first, but Sanchi was preserved better.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.sub_topic: Another name for the Harappan civilisation
questions.question: The Harappan civilisation is also known as the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Indus valley civilisation
Why: It is also called the Indus valley civilisation, after the river along which many of its sites lie.
Why not the others: (A) Vedic culture came later. (B) The Ganga valley was not its centre. (D) Mesopotamia was a separate civilisation in West Asia.
Key point: Harappan sites spread well beyond the Indus valley, to Gujarat, Haryana and Afghanistan.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.sub_topic: Two kinds of content in the epic
questions.question: Historians usually divide the contents of the Mahabharata into two broad sections:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Narrative and didactic
Why: The Mahabharata has narrative sections, which tell stories, and didactic sections, which lay down norms.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the usual division.
Key point: The division is not watertight, because the didactic sections include stories and the narrative carries social messages.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.sub_topic: Chronology of Brahmanical texts and records
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) The *Manusmriti* is compiled
(B) The Mandasor inscription of the silk weavers is engraved
(C) The Purusha sukta is composed as part of the Rigveda
(D) The Dharmasutras begin to be compiled
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: The Purusha sukta is part of the Rigveda (c. 1500–1000 BCE), and the Dharmasutras were compiled from c. 500 BCE. The *Manusmriti* dates to c. 200 BCE–200 CE, and the Mandasor inscription to the fifth century CE.
Why not the others: (A) puts the Dharmasutras before the Rigveda. (B) puts the *Manusmriti* before the Dharmasutras. (D) puts the inscription before the *Manusmriti*.
Key point: Inscriptions such as the Mandasor record let historians compare norms with actual practice.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Much of Colin Mackenzie's early information about the ruins at Hampi came from:
options: A) Priests of the Virupaksha temple
B) Officials of the Mughal court
D) Inscriptions in the Lotus Mahal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Priests of the Virupaksha temple
Why: Mackenzie relied on the memories of priests of the Virupaksha temple and the Pampadevi shrine.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were not his main sources.
Key point: Local memory, inscriptions and travellers' accounts were combined to study the city.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.sub_topic: Groups and officials in colonial records
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Group or official)
(A) Paharias
(B) Santhals
(C) Sahukars
(D) Collector

List-II (Description)
(I) Moneylenders and traders in the Deccan
(II) Hunters and shifting cultivators of the Rajmahal hills
(III) The Company official in charge of a district
(IV) Settled plough cultivators in the Damin-i-Koh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: The Paharias were hunters and shifting cultivators (II), and the Santhals settled plough cultivators (IV). Sahukars were Deccan moneylenders (I), and the Collector was in charge of a district (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the Paharias and the Santhals. (C) swaps the Santhals and the sahukars. (D) swaps the sahukars and the Collector.
Key point: Colonial records describe these groups from the viewpoint of revenue and order.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about how 1857 was represented:
(A) British pictures often celebrated the British as saviours and showed the rebels as savage.
(B) Twentieth-century nationalists hailed the revolt as the First War of Independence.
(C) Indian nationalists dismissed the revolt as a mere mutiny with no lessons.
(D) Rani Lakshmi Bai was shown in nationalist imagery as a masculine warrior on horseback.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT. British images celebrated the British, and nationalists celebrated the revolt and its heroes.
Why not the others: (C) is false. Nationalists drew inspiration from 1857. Options (A), (C) and (D) include (C).
Key point: Images of the same events differed sharply depending on who made them.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question:
Read the following source passage and answer the question that follows.

The Prayaga prashasti was composed in Sanskrit by Harisena, a court poet who also held high office under Samudragupta. It was inscribed on an Ashokan pillar at Allahabad, so an old pillar came to carry the praise of a much later king.

Harisena presents his master as a ruler without equal. The kings of Aryavarta, in the north, were uprooted and their lands taken over. The rulers of Dakshinapatha, in the south, were captured and then, by the king's grace, released. Frontier states and forest peoples paid tribute and came to the court, while distant rulers, among them the Shakas and the ruler of Sri Lanka, sought his favour. Samudragupta is compared to the gods and praised as a poet and a skilled musician.

Historians value such texts but read them with care. A prashasti was composed by a poet at the court to praise his patron, so it is silent about defeats and tends to magnify victories. Its claims have to be checked against other evidence, such as coins and other inscriptions.

Question: According to the passage, the Prayaga prashasti was composed by:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Harisena
Why: The passage says that Harisena, a court poet who held high office, composed the prashasti.
Why not the others: (A) Kalidasa was a poet and playwright. (B) Banabhatta wrote the *Harshacharita*. (D) Kautilya is linked with the *Arthashastra*.
Key point: Harisena also held official titles, which shows that court poets could be powerful men.

Question: Where was the Prayaga prashasti inscribed?
options: A) On an Ashokan pillar at Allahabad
B) On a cave wall at Ajanta
C) On copper plates at Pataliputra
D) On a rock at Junagadh
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) On an Ashokan pillar at Allahabad
Why: The passage says it was inscribed on an Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are not mentioned. (D) Junagadh has Rudradaman's inscription.
Key point: The same pillar carries Ashoka's edicts and, centuries later, Samudragupta's praise.

Question: According to the prashasti, what happened to the rulers of Dakshinapatha?
options: A) They were all killed in battle
B) Their lands were given to Brahmanas
C) They were exiled to Sri Lanka
D) They were captured, then released
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) They were captured, then released
Why: The passage says the rulers of the south were captured and then, by the king's grace, released.
Why not the others: (A) The northern kings were uprooted, not the southern ones killed. (B) and (C) are not in the passage.
Key point: Releasing defeated kings let the poet present the king as both powerful and generous.

Question: In which language was the Prayaga prashasti composed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Sanskrit
Why: The passage says the prashasti was composed in Sanskrit.
Why not the others: (A) Most Ashokan inscriptions were in Prakrit. (C) Pali was the language of the Buddhist canon. (D) Tamil was used in the south.

questions.sub_topic: Why historians read prashastis with care
questions.question:
Read the following source passage and answer the question that follows.

Question: Why, according to the passage, do historians treat the claims of a prashasti with caution?
options: A) Because the prashasti was written centuries later
B) Because it was written in an unknown script
C) Because court poets praised and exaggerated
D) Because it records only temple donations
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because court poets praised and exaggerated
Why: A prashasti was written by a court poet to praise his patron, so it is silent about defeats and magnifies victories.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are not true of the Prayaga prashasti. (D) It records conquests, not temple donations.
Key point: Coins and other inscriptions are used to check the claims of prashastis.
